title: FloodGuard Renewal Payment Statement: Amount Due for the New Term
content:
The renewal payment a named insured makes for a new term of the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy is the premium charged for the new term plus the policy fee charged for the new term, plus the balance the premium account shows from earlier terms, a balance owed being added and a credit being deducted.

## 1. The three lines of the statement

| Line | What it is | Where it is read |
|---|---|---|
| Premium for the new term | The premium charged on the premium account for the term that begins on the new term's start date | The premium charge on the premium account for that term |
| Policy fee for the new term | The policy fee charged on the premium account for that same term | The policy fee charge for that term |
| Balance from earlier terms | Every charge the premium account shows (premium charges, fees, returned payments, additional premium and refunds paid out) less every payment and credit it shows (payments received and return premium credited), leaving out the premium charge and the policy fee for the new term, rounded half-up to the cent | The whole premium account |

A balance from earlier terms that is owed is added to the payment; a balance from earlier terms that is a credit is deducted from it.

## 2. Whose credit enters

A credit balance from earlier terms that came from a payment by anyone other than the named insured is not deducted, because it is refunded to its payer instead. The payment a credit balance is taken to have come from is the most recent payment received on the premium account: when that payment was the named insured's own, the credit is deducted; when it was made by anyone else, such as the mortgagee paying from escrow, the credit does not enter the renewal payment. A balance owed from earlier terms always enters.

## 3. Assembling the payment

Every discount, dividend or credit on the renewal payment is worked out on the premium charged for the new term and rounded half-up to the cent on its own. The renewal payment is the premium charged for the new term, plus the policy fee charged for the new term, plus the balance that enters from earlier terms, less each such discount, dividend or credit, plus any late charge added to the payment, the whole rounded half-up to the cent.

## 4. Hypothetical statements

The figures below are hypothetical inputs chosen for illustration; they are not rates or fees of any tier.

- **Balance owed.** Premium charged for the new term 820.00; policy fee charged for the new term 50.00; earlier terms leave 12.40 owed. The renewal payment is 820.00 plus 50.00 plus 12.40, which is 882.40.
- **Credit from the named insured's own payment.** Same premium and fee; earlier terms leave a credit of 25.00, and the most recent payment received was the named insured's. The credit is deducted: 820.00 plus 50.00 less 25.00, which is 845.00.
- **Credit from the mortgagee's escrow payment.** Same premium and fee; earlier terms leave a credit of 25.00, and the most recent payment received was the mortgagee's. The credit does not enter: 820.00 plus 50.00, which is 870.00.
- **Nothing left from earlier terms.** Premium 820.00 and fee 50.00 with a zero earlier balance give 870.00.
